Author: @OnePlayer480
Comment Text:
​ @unoriginalperson72  Because Bethesda had to release Skyrim, feature complete, on XBOX 360 and PS3. And the DVD discs had a limited amount of storage, and the console, unlike a PC, had only so much memory and processing power, and it still had to render everything.

So, Bethesda had to make a bunch of solutions to make the game not need to make so many unnecessary calculations and rendering.

One of the many cases of that is dragons falling. It is not random, Bethesda created a bunch of "landing zones" at which Dragons would fall and slide onto so the game doesn't have to make a huge crater or later static objects temporarily with new terrain that has to be accounted for. Instead, the terrain that can be altered is set in stone and will be used only if a Dragon needs to land in that area.

This is why in some places, Dragons fall all the way behind a mountain or completely disappear at first glance.

They did fall, but not anywhere close, because where you were fighting it, there was nowhere for it to fall, no designated area. Or the check failed and the dragon had to fall in a different area because of Bugthesda reasons.

Comment Text: It’s actually a problem with camera positioning. If you’ve ever switched from first to third person you’d notice your character jitters a bit, especially if they have their weapons drawn. That’s because the camera is adjusting where you’re actually looking. For killcams it works the same way, so if you’re in first person it adjusts your aim going into third person. If your projectile would strike dead center of their chest, the jitter would cause it to hit their stomach of even miss entirely. It’s such a stupid thing, but it ruins mage builds where your ammo recharges after about 20 seconds compared to knocking another arrow in 2.

That’s easy to fix.
Look at starting skills.
You have 5 minor skills (20)
You have 1 major skill (25)

Starting position, if no turn, try all the way to the left, if no turn try all the ày to the right. If no turn exit lockpicking mode and re-enter lockpicking mode.
